subject: Emergency: ModelX.Lite latency divergence — request fallback + rollback authorization
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] ModelX.Lite p50/p95 divergence spike — initial findings

Team —

Observed a sustained p95 tail increase for model tag mx-lite@2026-10-29 across the US pool starting ~17:40 PDT. Quick summary: 

- p50 increased from ~90ms -> 160ms (short spike)
- p95 increased from ~220ms -> 1.1s (sustained for ~25m)
- error rate steady (0.1%), no request timeouts
- traffic distribution: 88% hosted API; small % on Dedicated for FinNova

Attachments: latency_digests_20261030.pdf (digest), trace_summary_20261030.json (sample traces).

Immediate mitigations we kicked:
- Enabled aggressive KV cache warmup on a subset of hosts (reduced p50 by ~30ms)
- Automated fallback to mx-lite@2026-10-22 (older quantized build) triggered for canary (5%)

Observations: fallback canary shows p95 dropping back to ~240ms. However, for FinNova-specific Dedicated pool we do not have automatic fallback path (customer pinned variant). They are seeing the full regression.

Asking for:
1) Business authorization to divert FinNova traffic to the older variant for up to 2 hours while we root cause (requires Sales/AE sign-off due to SLA carveout).
2) If diversion unacceptable, we need permission to roll back the hosted deployment tag mx-lite@2026-10-29 to mx-lite@2026-10-22 immediately (will trigger a short redeploy, ~8m).

Why urgent: FinNova is high-priority (D-77421) and traffic is originating from their primary region; we risk an SLA credit if unaddressed for >30m.

Dev
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 18:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Alert] ModelX.Lite p50/p95 divergence spike — initial findings

Naomi / Rishi —

Heads-up from SRE: FinNova Dedicated pool is experiencing the p95 spike tied to mx-lite@2026-10-29. They are a renewal-in-flight account (see deal D-77421). We need quick commercial sign-off to either: 

- Divert their dedicated traffic to mx-lite@2026-10-22 (temporary fallback), or
- Approve immediate rollback of hosted tag (mx-lite@2026-10-29 -> mx-lite@2026-10-22).

If Sales cannot accept diversion (customer policy on pinned variants), we should roll back the hosted tag and coordinate with FinNova ops. The rollback will cost ~8m downtime on deployment control plane operations and may require a short SLA carveout.

Please confirm asap so we can action. If I don't hear back in 20 minutes, we'll plan for the rollback and notify FinNova ops.

Avery
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Avery / team —

I've reviewed the traces (trace_summary_20261030.json) — the regression appears to be a small attention-kernel regression combined with longer KV cache warmups for sequences with specialized tokenizers coming from FinNova traffic. Root-cause fix will likely need a small kernel patch and retest (2-4 hours).

My recommendation (operational):
- Approve temporary diversion of FinNova to mx-lite@2026-10-22 for up to 2 hours. This is low-risk and reversible.
- If diversion blocked by customer policy, approve a roll back of the hosted tag. We will coordinate an immediate redeploy window (target ~8-10 minutes of deployment churn).

I approve the technical rollback path; need Sales to authorize the customer-impact decision.

Marcus
